links.comparator_used: Simulated baseline retention among the same high-risk patients with no intervention (not universal or random allocation)
links.outcome: Twelve-month ART retention among patients classified as high risk by the ML model (n = 512)
links.effect: Baseline retention 44.1%. Combined package raised it to 64.0% (RR = 1.45; p < 0.001), an absolute gain of 19.9 percentage points. Individual interventions: Expert Client support 55.0% (RR = 1.25), two-way texting 52.7% (RR = 1.19). Among newly initiated patients retention rose from 43.0% to 58.9% (RR = 1.37), and among clinically unstable patients from 28.3% to 39.1% (RR = 1.38).
links.tradeoff: 46% of high-risk patients remained hard to retain after multiple interventions. Their expected retention rose only from about 0.15 to 0.20, and it was worst among patients who were virally unsuppressed, had depressive symptoms, or were younger. Effects among adolescents were more modest (34.3% to 45.6%; RR = 1.33). Results come from a simulation that used meta-analytic effect sizes.
links.quote: Machine learning–guided targeting of ART retention interventions can substantially improve retention outcomes, particularly when interventions are combined.

design_hint: risk-based targeting of interventions using predicted risk threshold
